extracted.intended_audience: general readers of literary fiction (readers of H.G. Wells / novel readers)
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a novel (literary fiction) describing characters, scenes, and a newspaper-style account of Julian Felsenburgh's arrival and oratorical effect on a mass audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual oratory / linguistic mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: “All languages seem the same to him; he delivered speeches during the eight months through which the Eastern Convention lasted, in no less than fifteen tongues.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a key attribute of Felsenburgh's greatness: facility in many languages is treated as evidence of universal appeal and capability to address diverse audiences directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of audiences / human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: “He showed also ... the most astonishing knowledge, not only of human nature, but of every trait under which that divine thing manifests itself. He appeared acquainted with the history, the prejudices, the fears, the hopes, the expectations of all the innumerable sects and castes of the East to whom it was his business to speak.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being deeply informed about the histories, prejudices and expectations of target groups is presented as essential for persuasive leadership and oratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral integrity / absence of discreditable conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: “He has been guilty of none of those crimes--there is not one that convicts him of sin--those crimes of the Yellow Press, of corruption, of commercial or political bullying which have so stained the past of all those old politicians...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative treats lack of scandal, corruption, or opportunistic behavior as an important evaluative criterion for a modern leader's legitimacy and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-partisanship / not forming a party
rubrics_metrics.description: “Mr. FELSENBURGH has not even formed a party. He, and not his underlings, have conquered.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding formal party affiliation and appearing above faction is depicted as contributing to universal authority and broad acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and brevity of message
rubrics_metrics.description: “the speech, delivered in Esperanto, was a very simple one, and very short. It consisted of a brief announcement of the great fact of Universal Brotherhood...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, simple message (here: Universal Brotherhood) is shown as maximally effective in moving a vast audience; reporters emphasize the speech's simplicity as part of its power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrained physical presence and clear delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: “he stood motionless with his hands on the rail, he made but one gesture that drew a kind of sob from the crowd, he spoke these words slowly, distinctly, and in a clear voice;”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controlled, minimal gestures and deliberate, distinct speech are framed as producing outsized emotional impact — restraint amplifies authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to produce unified mass emotional response
rubrics_metrics.description: “a profound silence dominated ... Many were weeping silently, the lips of thousands moved without a sound, and all faces were turned to that simple figure ... the eyes of many, centuries ago, were turned on one known now to history as JESUS OF NAZARETH.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliciting collective silence, tears, and unified attention is presented as the ultimate evidence of charismatic oratorical success and perceived messianic significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public spectacle / ritualized appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: “The white volor ... the volor began that wonderful parade which London will never forget. Four times during the night Mr. FELSENBURGH went round the enormous metropolis, speaking no word; and everywhere the groan preceded and followed him, while silence accompanied his actual passage.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonverbal spectacle and repeated ceremonial appearances are credited with reinforcing awe and consolidating public perception of authority even without further speech.
